data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a small overall favourable prior-year reserve movement of GBP 1.922m (a release of c.0.83% of opening gross claims reserves). The movement arose from overall favourable claims development, notably a GBP 5.89m improvement on reinsurance acceptances, partially offset by adverse development in Marine (GBP 1.621m) and Property (Fire and other damage to property) (GBP 2.094m). Prior large events such as Superstorm Sandy and other 2012 losses have previously driven reserve volatility but recent re-underwriting and benign experience have driven improvements.
raw_causal_phrases: An overall improvement of GBP 1,922,000 on prior year's provisions was experienced during the year.

An improvement of GBP 5,890,000 on reinsurance acceptances was partially offset by deteriorations of GBP 1,621,000 on marine, aviation and transport and GBP 2,094,000 on fire and other damage to property.

It is the reduced level of losses, as a result of the re-underwriting that began to be implemented late in 2011 and on into 2012, that has continued to keep attrition below expectation for this year thus improving the actual return above levels previously predicted.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year movement taken from note 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' (explicitly states GBP 1,922,000 improvement). The note gives component amounts for reinsurance acceptances and two classes; these were used as gross amounts as printed. No gross claims development triangle was present in the annual accounts (claims development table not provided), so the movement note is used as the primary source. Some named events are referenced in the Managing Agent's Report; amounts for those events are not quantified in the report. RITC items are present elsewhere in the underwriting-year accounts but do not appear to distort the Movement-in-prior-year note used here.
